name: Peroneal Tendon Subluxation / Dislocation
definition: Instability of the peroneal tendons behind the lateral malleolus, typically due to superior peroneal retinaculum injury.

investigations.principle: Dynamic ultrasound is especially useful; MRI assesses retinaculum and tendon injury.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, tendon, cartilage, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Recurrent symptomatic dislocation commonly requires surgical stabilization.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Gulpha-Snayu instability phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Instability of the peroneal tendons behind the lateral malleolus, typically due to superior peroneal retinaculum injury.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, severe deformity, progressive weakness, tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
